item.text:
# 2B.5 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** The record is **modestly favorable**. Scholz did try to restrain an ally/arms recipient, especially Israel, through ceasefire calls, humanitarian-law language, and warnings against a Rafah offensive. He also avoided turning German support for Ukraine into a proxy-war mandate. The main limitation is that Germany had no militias or proxy forces of its own, so evidence is mostly indirect and diplomatic rather than operational.

## Accepted claim items

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Joint Statement on Gaza** | Federal Government | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/joint-statement-from-the-leaders-of-the-united-states-argentina-austria-brazil-bulgaria-canada-colombia-denmark-france-germany-poland-portugal-romania-serbia-spain-thailand-and-the-united-kingdom-on-gaza-2290942 | Scholz joined a statement calling for an immediate ceasefire, unconditional hostage release, protection of civilians, large-scale humanitarian aid, and compliance with international humanitarian law. It also opposed annexation and backed a negotiated two-state outcome. This is the clearest direct evidence that he tried to restrain an ally/partner from escalatory or unlawful conduct. | 2B.5, 2B.4 |
| **Interview des Bundeskanzlers mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz said he had warned against a Rafah ground offensive, insisted that more humanitarian aid had to reach Gaza, and said every arms delivery was carefully assessed in advance. This supports a view that he tried to apply proportionality and civilian-protection constraints to an arms recipient. | 2B.5, 2B.4, 2B.1 |
| **Summer press conference with Federal Chancellor Scholz** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040 | Scholz said Israel has the right to defend itself, but warfare must comply with international humanitarian law and humanitarian aid must reach Gaza on a large scale. He also reiterated support for a two-state solution. This is explicit restraint language directed at an ally/recipient rather than a blank check. | 2B.5, 2B.4, 2B.3 |
| **Video: Anniversary of the 7 October attack** | Federal Government | 7 Oct 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/media-center/chancellor-kanzler-kompakt-2313552 | Scholz called for a ceasefire one year after the Hamas attack and described the war as a disaster for the Palestinian people. This is indirect, but it shows continued pressure toward de-escalation and civilian protection. | 2B.5, 2B.4, 2B.1 |
| **Interview des Bundeskanzlers mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz also affirmed Israel’s right to defend itself and said Germany remained in close contact with Israel while continuing arms support. This is the main counterweight: he did not fully suspend support or impose hard public conditionality, so restraint existed but was limited. | 2B.5, 2B.4 |
| **Scholz im Interview mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz said fear of escalation is understandable, rejected a quick endgame by force, and framed support for Ukraine as necessary to prevent Russian victory. This is relevant because it shows he did not treat Ukrainian support as a license for proxy escalation. | 2B.5, 2B.1, 2B.3 |

## Counterevidence / limitations

- I found **no reliable evidence** that Scholz knowingly enabled atrocities by a proxy, militia, or client force.
- I also found **no evidence** that Germany had direct control over militias or security forces in a way comparable to states with proxy networks.
- The strongest limitation is that the response was mostly **diplomatic restraint**, not direct command-and-control over recipients’ battlefield behavior.

## Synthesis for 2B.5

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz did try to restrain an ally/arms recipient from destabilizing or unlawful conduct, especially on Gaza.
- **Why:** he backed ceasefire language, humanitarian access, IHL compliance, and warnings against an offensive likely to increase civilian harm.
- **Main caveat:** he continued support and contact rather than imposing maximal conditionality, so this is restraint, not coercive control.
- **Overall:** mildly positive on 2B.5, with evidence concentrated on Israel/Gaza rather than on proxies or militias.

## Search gap

- I found **little direct evidence** on prisoner treatment or on formal responsibility for proxy conduct, because Germany was not running proxy forces in 2024.
- Evidence on “militias, proxies, clients” is therefore mostly absent rather than negative.
